title: Jeremiah Chapter 48 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 48 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 48 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 48.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 48, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully
questions.correctAnswer: Woe unto Nebo
questions.explanation: Woe unto Nebo is mentioned first in Jeremiah 48:1 before the other events or statements.

questions.question: Who does the LORD of hosts say is confounded and taken in Jeremiah 48?
questions.correctAnswer: Kiriathaim
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:1 states that Kiriathaim is confounded and taken.

questions.question: What have they devised against Moab in Heshbon according to Jeremiah 48?
questions.correctAnswer: Evil
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:2 states that in Heshbon they have devised evil against Moab.

questions.question: From where shall a voice of crying come, announcing spoiling and great destruction?
questions.correctAnswer: Horonaim
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:3 says a voice of crying shall be from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction.

questions.question: What is said about Moab's little ones in Jeremiah 48?
options: They have caused a cry to be heard
questions.correctAnswer: They have caused a cry to be heard
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:4 states that Moab's little ones have caused a cry to be heard.

questions.question: What is the instruction given in Jeremiah 48 regarding saving lives?
options: Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:6 commands to flee and save lives, comparing to the heath in the wilderness.

questions.question: Who will go forth into captivity with his priests and princes according to Jeremiah 48?
questions.correctAnswer: Chemosh
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:7 states that Chemosh shall go forth into captivity with his priests and princes.

questions.question: What will happen to every city in Moab as per Jeremiah 48?
options: The spoiler shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape
questions.correctAnswer: The spoiler shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:8 says the spoiler shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape.

questions.question: What is the condition of the cities of Moab in Jeremiah 48?
options: The cities shall be desolate, without any to dwell therein
The cities shall be filled with refugees
questions.correctAnswer: The cities shall be desolate, without any to dwell therein
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:9 commands to give wings unto Moab that it may flee because the cities shall be desolate with no inhabitants.

questions.question: What curse is pronounced in Jeremiah 48?
options: Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully
Cursed be those who trust in their treasures
Cursed be the cities that fall
Cursed be the enemies of Moab
questions.correctAnswer: Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:10 pronounces a curse on those who do the work of the LORD deceitfully and those who keep back their sword from blood.

questions.question: What has Moab been since his youth according to Jeremiah 48?
options: At ease and settled on his lees
questions.correctAnswer: At ease and settled on his lees
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:11 says Moab has been at ease from his youth and settled on his lees.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 48 says that Moab's calamity is near to come and his affliction hasteth fast.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:16 clearly states the calamity of Moab is near to come and his affliction hasteth fast.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 48 says Chemosh will go forth into captivity with his priests and princes.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:7 states that Chemosh shall go forth into captivity with his priests and princes.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 48 says Moab shall prosper and their cities will not be destroyed.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:8-9 clearly states that the spoiler shall come upon every city and the cities shall be desolate.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 48 says Nebo will be honored and rise victorious.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:1 states 'Woe unto Nebo! for it is spoiled,' indicating Nebo will not be honored or victorious.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 48 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 48 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 48:17, what is broken and described as beautiful?
options: The strong staff and the beautiful rod
The city walls and the gates
questions.correctAnswer: The strong staff and the beautiful rod
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:17 says, 'How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!' indicating these are broken.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 48:18 promise will happen if the daughter that inhabits Dibon does not come down from her glory?
options: The spoiler of Moab will come and destroy her strong holds
She will be exalted above all nations
She will find peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: The spoiler of Moab will come and destroy her strong holds
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:18 warns that the spoiler shall come upon Dibon and destroy her strong holds if she does not come down from her glory.

questions.question: What is the reaction Jeremiah 48:20 says Moab should have because it is broken down?
questions.correctAnswer: Howl and cry
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:20 commands to 'howl and cry' because Moab is confounded and broken down.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 48:21 and 48:22 together describe the extent of judgment on Moab?
options: Judgment comes on the plain country and specific cities like Dibon and Nebo
Only the mountainous regions are spared
Only the cities near the sea are judged
Judgment is limited to the capital city
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment comes on the plain country and specific cities like Dibon and Nebo
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:21 mentions judgment upon the plain country, and 48:22 lists cities including Dibon and Nebo, showing widespread judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 48:25 describe the fate of Moab's power?
options: The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken
Moab will be exalted among nations
Moab will build a mighty army
questions.correctAnswer: The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:25 states 'The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken,' indicating loss of power.

questions.question: What practical lesson can Christians learn from Jeremiah 48:26 about pride against the Lord?
options: Pride leads to humiliation and derision
Pride is a sign of strength
questions.correctAnswer: Pride leads to humiliation and derision
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:26 says Moab is made drunk because he magnified himself against the LORD and shall be in derision, teaching humility is vital.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 48:27, what was Moab's attitude toward Israel, and what is the warning implied?
options: Moab mocked Israel, but will face judgment
Moab helped Israel in times of need
questions.correctAnswer: Moab mocked Israel, but will face judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:27 states Israel was a derision to Moab, but the context warns Moab's pride will not stand.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 48:28 advise the inhabitants of Moab to do in times of danger?
options: Leave the cities and dwell in the rock like a dove
questions.correctAnswer: Leave the cities and dwell in the rock like a dove
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:28 instructs the people to leave cities and be like the dove nesting in rocks for safety.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 48:29 characterize Moab's attitude before judgment came?
questions.correctAnswer: Pride, loftiness, arrogancy, and haughtiness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:29 lists Moab's pride and arrogance as reasons for impending judgment.

questions.question: What assurance does Jeremiah 48:30 give about God's knowledge and judgment of Moab's wrath?
options: God knows Moab's wrath but his lies will not prevail
God is unaware of Moab's actions
questions.correctAnswer: God knows Moab's wrath but his lies will not prevail
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:30 states the LORD knows Moab's wrath but declares it will not succeed because of lies.

questions.question: How can Christians apply Jeremiah 48:31 about mourning for others in distress?
options: We should mourn and pray for those facing judgment or hardship
We should rejoice over others' failures
questions.correctAnswer: We should mourn and pray for those facing judgment or hardship
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:31 shows God mourning for Moab, teaching believers to have compassion and intercession for others.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 48:32 metaphorically compare to the destruction of Moab's produce?
options: The vine of Sibmah and its summer fruits and vintage
questions.correctAnswer: The vine of Sibmah and its summer fruits and vintage
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:32 compares the spoil of Moab to the destruction of the vine of Sibmah and its harvest.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 48:10 curses those who do the work of the LORD deceitfully and those who withhold their sword from blood.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:10 states 'Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood.'

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 48:13 says Moab will be ashamed of Israel, as Israel was ashamed of Bethel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:13 says Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, not Israel; Israel was ashamed of Bethel, so the statement is incorrect.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 48:9 says that all cities of Moab shall be filled with inhabitants and flourish.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:9 says 'the cities thereof shall be desolate, without any to dwell therein,' so the statement is false.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 48 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 48.

questions.question: What has been taken from the plentiful field of Moab according to Jeremiah 48:33?
questions.correctAnswer: Joy and gladness
questions.explanation: This is stated in Jeremiah 48:33, where it mentions, 'And joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field, and from the land of Moab...'

questions.question: What does the Lord promise to cause to cease in Moab as stated in Jeremiah 48:35?
questions.correctAnswer: Offering in high places
questions.explanation: According to Jeremiah 48:35, 'Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab, saith the LORD, him that offereth in the high places...'

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 48:38, how has the Lord described Moab?
options: Like a vessel wherein is no pleasure
questions.correctAnswer: Like a vessel wherein is no pleasure
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:38 states, 'for I have broken Moab like a vessel wherein is no pleasure...'

questions.question: What metaphor is used to describe the hearts of the mighty men of Moab in Jeremiah 48:41?
options: As the heart of a woman in her pangs
questions.correctAnswer: As the heart of a woman in her pangs
questions.explanation: This metaphor is found in Jeremiah 48:41, which states, 'the mighty men's hearts in Moab at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.'

questions.question: What is said to come forth out of Heshbon according to Jeremiah 48:45?
questions.correctAnswer: A fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:45 mentions, 'but a fire shall come forth out of Heshbon...'

questions.question: Which group of people is mentioned as perishing in Jeremiah 48:46?
questions.correctAnswer: The people of Moab
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 48:46, it states, 'Woe be unto thee, O Moab! the people of Chemosh perisheth...'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Chemosh' in Jeremiah 48:46 refer to?
questions.correctAnswer: A god of Moab
questions.explanation: The word 'Chemosh' refers to the chief god of the Moabites, as mentioned in Jeremiah 48:46.

questions.question: What literary device is employed in Jeremiah 48:33-34 to express lamentation?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The verses exhibit parallelism by repeating related ideas, enhancing the expression of lamentation.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of judgment against Moab as seen in Jeremiah 48:42?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 15:1
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:1 speaks of the judgment against Moab, similar to Jeremiah 48:42 which states Moab shall be destroyed.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the prophecy of Moab's downfall as indicated in Jeremiah 48:39?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 18:2
questions.explanation: Revelation 18:2 describes the fall of Babylon, paralleling the judgment themes found in Jeremiah 48:39.

questions.question: What comes before Jeremiah 48:33 in the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: The lamentation over Moab
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:32-33 discusses the lamentation over Moab before verse 33.

questions.question: What does the term 'desolate' in Jeremiah 48:34 signify about the waters of Nimrim?
questions.correctAnswer: They are dried up
questions.explanation: The term 'desolate' implies a lack of water, indicating the waters of Nimrim are dried up as stated in Jeremiah 48:34.

questions.question: The judgment against Moab, as described in Jeremiah 48, is a result of what action according to Jeremiah 48:42?
questions.correctAnswer: Magnifying self against the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:42 indicates that Moab shall be destroyed 'because he hath magnified himself against the LORD.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 48:47, the captivity of Moab will never be restored.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:47 states, 'Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days...,' indicating restoration is promised.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 48:40 describes a coming destruction for Moab without hope of recovery.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: While Jeremiah 48:40 describes judgment, it does not indicate a lack of future hope, as restoration is mentioned in verse 47.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 48 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 48 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 48:10 teach about God's nature in relation to justice and judgment?
options: God curses those who perform His work deceitfully
God rewards those who keep peace at all costs
God ignores deceit in His service
God shows favor to those who avoid violence
questions.correctAnswer: God curses those who perform His work deceitfully
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:10 states, 'Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully,' showing God's just nature in condemning false service.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sinfulness and pride is taught in Jeremiah 48:29?
options: Moab's pride and haughtiness lead to divine judgment
Pride is rewarded with peace and prosperity
Haughtiness is a sign of divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Moab's pride and haughtiness lead to divine judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:29 condemns Moab's arrogance and pride, linking human pride to coming judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 48:47 teach concerning God's plan for restoration after judgment?
options: God promises to restore Moab’s captivity in the latter days
God permanently rejects the nations that sin
There is no hope after divine judgment
Restoration is based solely on human effort
questions.correctAnswer: God promises to restore Moab’s captivity in the latter days
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:47 states, 'Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days,' teaching God's redemptive restoration.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 48:30 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:30 says, 'I know his wrath,' demonstrating God's omniscience in fully knowing human dispositions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated in Jeremiah 48:44 through God's control over judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:44 portrays God bringing the year of visitation upon Moab, showing His sovereign control over history.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 48:7 connect to the broader biblical theme of idolatry’s consequences?
options: Idolatry leads to captivity and defeat, as Chemosh and his priests are taken into exile
Idolatry guarantees divine blessing and protection
Idolatry is overlooked when accompanied by wealth
Idolatry is only a minor offense compared to other sins
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry leads to captivity and defeat, as Chemosh and his priests are taken into exile
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:7 describes Chemosh going into captivity with his priests, illustrating the biblical principle that idolatry results in judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 48:25 prepare for New Testament teachings on the consequences of pride before God?
options: The horn and arm of Moab are broken, symbolizing God's judgment on pride
Pride is shown as a virtue leading to exaltation
God ignores pride in foreign nations
Pride is unrelated to divine punishment
questions.correctAnswer: The horn and arm of Moab are broken, symbolizing God's judgment on pride
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:25’s imagery of broken strength prefigures New Testament warnings about pride leading to downfall (cf. James 4:6).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 48:11 and 48:12 teach about human complacency and divine discipline?
options: Complacency leads to divine discipline that empties and breaks vessels
Complacency brings lasting peace without consequence
Divine discipline is unrelated to human behavior
Human effort can prevent divine discipline
questions.correctAnswer: Complacency leads to divine discipline that empties and breaks vessels
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:11 shows Moab’s complacency, and 48:12 predicts God sending wanderers to empty and break their vessels, symbolizing discipline.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 48:35 and 48:46 teach about idolatry and its consequences?
options: Idolatry leads to the cessation of sacrifices and the captivity of people
Idolatry is ultimately beneficial for a nation
Idolatry is tolerated by God without judgment
Idolatry results in material wealth and security
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry leads to the cessation of sacrifices and the captivity of people
questions.explanation: Verse 35 promises the end of offerings to false gods, and verse 46 describes the captivity of Moab’s people, linking idolatry to judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 48:31 and 48:36 reveal about God’s emotional response to judgment on sinners?
options: God mourns and laments over the destruction of His people
God is indifferent to the fate of sinners
God rejoices in the downfall of sinners
God’s heart is hardened against sinners
questions.correctAnswer: God mourns and laments over the destruction of His people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:31 and 48:36 describe God’s heart sounding like pipes and mourning, showing His compassionate grief over judgment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jeremiah 48:42-44 teaches that God's judgment is unfair and arbitrary. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God’s judgment is the result of Moab’s pride and magnification against Him, demonstrating just retribution
God punishes Moab without cause or reason
Judgment is random and unrelated to behavior
God’s judgment is based solely on political considerations
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is the result of Moab’s pride and magnification against Him, demonstrating just retribution
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:42-44 links Moab’s destruction to its pride against the LORD, showing that judgment is just and deserved.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice does Jeremiah 48:26 teach concerning the fate of nations who magnify themselves against God?
options: Such nations are made drunk and mocked, illustrating humiliation as part of divine justice
Such nations escape punishment through pride
God rewards prideful nations with honor
Humiliation is unrelated to divine justice
questions.correctAnswer: Such nations are made drunk and mocked, illustrating humiliation as part of divine justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:26 describes Moab wallowing in vomit and derision due to self-exaltation against God, showing humiliation is a judicial consequence.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly emphasized in Jeremiah 48:38 by the metaphor of a broken vessel?
questions.correctAnswer: Wrath
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:38 depicts Moab as a broken vessel 'wherein is no pleasure,' highlighting God’s wrath against sin.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 48:16 contribute to the thematic development of impending divine judgment in prophetic literature?
options: It emphasizes the imminence and urgency of Moab’s calamity
It downplays the seriousness of judgment
It suggests judgment will be delayed indefinitely
It denies that Moab will experience affliction
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the imminence and urgency of Moab’s calamity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48:16 states, 'The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hasteth fast,' stressing urgency in prophetic judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 48:18 and 48:39 teach about the consequences of misplaced confidence in human strongholds?
options: False security in strongholds leads to shame and derision when God breaks them
Confidence in cities is a sign of true faith
God rewards those who trust in physical defenses
questions.correctAnswer: False security in strongholds leads to shame and derision when God breaks them
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 39 show Moab’s strongholds destroyed and the nation turned to derision, teaching the futility of trusting in human defenses.
